datafield.subfield: "Mother:Wife:Student:Designer:Sister:Daughter. In life, how does one person manage many different roles[facets]? Ideally, the best way to manage the multiple factes of one's life would be to step away from one facet to focus on another. However, that would only work if people were machines. In reality, such a devout focus is nearly impossible and the constant overlap of out many roles can fuel an intense inner chaos invisible to the outside world. Sifting through chaos to create a sense of order directly relates to the role of a graphic designer. As designers, it is our role to create order from a disordered world and then present this order to the world for its use. My intention of this book series is to fuse one facet of my life to another while allowing my thesis topic, Order and Chaos [in Graphic Design], to guide the narratives and inform my overall design." Artist Statement.

Three white paperback volumes. Text is printed in such a way that the book may be read from front to back or turned upside down and read from back to front to discover another facet. Each book contains two facets.
Covers made from cross-hatched reed material that has been dyed and printed upon.
